title: Dynamically protected erasure qubit via low-frequency charge driving
abstract: Dynamical protection via strong driving can enable resilient quantum processing on imperfect physical hardware. However, the practical utility of such schemes is frequently limited by parasitic processes such as drive-induced dephasing and leakage. Here, we demonstrate that sub-GHz charge driving of superconducting Kerr oscillators (KOs) in the transmon regime circumvents this trade-off, simultaneously activating fast parametric interactions and protecting the encoded qubit from low-frequency noise. The key is the frequency dependence of the charge sensitivity: using the AC Stark shift as a probe, we find that the KO frequency sensitivity to a charge drive grows quadratically with both drive frequency and amplitude, making the oscillator weakly sensitive to $1/f$ charge noise yet strongly coupled to drives near 1~GHz. Exploiting this, we first demonstrate cooling and reset of the KO in 82~ns, to a residual population below $0.7\%$---lower than its $2.5\%$ steady-state thermal population. Next, using two KOs, we demonstrate logical control and dynamical protection of a dual-rail qubit with nearly fourfold erasure bias. Finally, using a single end-of-circuit erasure check, we achieve an error per Clifford of $5.6\times10^{-4}$, which falls to $1.5\times10^{-4}$ after post-selection, with 25~ns gates.

bite.hook: Superconducting qubits cooled and reset in 82 ns to under 0.7% residual population using sub-GHz charge driving.
tldr: Demonstrated a dynamically protected erasure qubit using sub-GHz charge driving on superconducting Kerr oscillators.
Leveraged frequency dependence of charge sensitivity to remain weakly sensitive to 1/f charge noise while strongly coupled to ~1 GHz drives.
Achieved 82 ns cooling/reset, a fourfold erasure bias on a dual-rail qubit, and an error per Clifford of 1.5x10^-4 after post-selection.
bite.whyItMatters: Building fault-tolerant quantum computers requires protecting fragile qubits from environmental noise while still allowing fast, precise control. This work proves that clever low-frequency driving can achieve high-speed control and strong noise protection simultaneously.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to balance a spinning top while someone is shaking the table. By vibrating the table at a very specific rhythm, the researchers actually managed to stabilize the top against the shaking while still being able to steer it instantly.

glossary.shortDef: A qubit designed so that dominant errors convert into known erasures rather than unknown bit flips.
glossary.eli5Def: A special quantum bit that, when it gets confused, raises its hand to admit it rather than giving a silently wrong answer.

glossary.eli5Def: The way a laser or microwave field gently nudges the energy levels of an atom or circuit.
